'''Lightfoils''' were small and elegant [[energy sword]]s based upon [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] design.

==Description==
[[File:Tapani_lightfoils.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Two Tapani sector [[Tapani Noble Houses|Nobles]] dueling with lightfoils.]]

Originally designed in secret by the [[Sith/Legends|Sith]] of the [[Mecrosa Order]], the quality of the lightfoil was on par with that of [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] lightsabers. Each one was a work of art, lightweight and balanced. It was wielded with one hand as its petite and elegantly designed handles attested. They were best suited for use with one hand in the graceful [[Form II/Legends|Form II: Makashi]] style.<ref name="JATM" />

After the [[Cleansing of the Nine Houses]], with the Sith gone, so-called modern lightfoils began to be made and used by non-[[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]], becoming popular among certain nobles of the [[Tapani sector/Legends|Tapani sector]], especially those that called themselves "[[Saber rake/Legends|saber rakes]]." However, these post-Cleansing lightfoils were weaker than the authentic or "archaic" lightfoils due to the poor quality [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|focusing crystals]] used in their manufacture and the relatively low level of craftsmanship compared to [[Jedi artisan/Legends|Jedi artisans]]. However, the knockoff lightfoils apparently did not require any connection to [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to create, and were fully usable by non-Force sensitives.<ref name="JATM" />

==History==
The original or "archaic" lightfoils were popular in the years leading up to the [[Great Sith War/Legends|Great Sith War]]. After the decline of the Sith in the Tapani Sector, the less potent "modern" lightfoils that were constructed were popular among Tapani Sector nobles, who would pay large sums of money to obtain them.<ref name="JATM" /><ref name="Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref>
